framework: China - Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services (Order No. 15, in force 15 Aug 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: On finding illegal content, providers must stop generation/transmission, remove content, retrain or optimise the model, and report to authorities.
what_is_tested: Post-deployment content violations

framework: China - Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Order No. 21; promulgated 10 Apr 2026; in force 15 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must run a security assessment and report to provincial cyberspace authority on launch, major technical change, reaching 1 million registered users or 100,000 monthly active users, or other triggers; assessment focuses on safeguards, training data, extreme-situation response, minors and older adults.
what_is_tested: Security assessment of companion-type AI

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Instructions for use must state the accuracy level and metrics, robustness and cybersecurity levels against which the system was tested and validated, plus known circumstances affecting them.
what_is_tested: Disclosure of tested performance, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Provider must draw up an EU declaration of conformity per high-risk system, keep it available for 10 years, and by drawing it up assumes responsibility for compliance with Section 2.
what_is_tested: Formal declaration of conformity

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: The Commission may fine GPAI providers up to 3% of worldwide turnover or EUR 15 million for infringements, failing to provide information, failing to comply with Art. 93 measures, or failing to give model access for evaluation.
what_is_tested: Penalty exposure for GPAI providers

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Safety mitigations must be robust under adversarial pressure, and signatories carry out post-market monitoring (feedback channels, incident forms, bug bounties and similar) to inform whether the risk stays acceptable.
what_is_tested: Mitigation robustness; post-release monitoring

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Technical report surveying how trust in AI can be built through transparency, explainability and controllability, engineering pitfalls and threats, and approaches to assessing and improving properties such as resilience, safety, security and privacy; does not define trustworthiness levels; published 28 May 2020, 43 pages.
what_is_tested: Trustworthiness properties overview

framework: Japan AISI - Guide to Red Teaming Methodology on AI Safety v1.10 (31 Mar 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes three processes: planning and preparation; developing and conducting attack scenarios; reporting results and improvement plans, in 15 steps.
what_is_tested: Prompt injection, prompt leaking, poisoning, evasion, model extraction, membership inference, model inversion; risk scenarios from seven evaluation perspectives (Sec. 7.1)
who_tests: Internal red team or third party; attack planner independent of development manager (Sec. 4)

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree of the AI Framework Act (Presidential Decree No. 36053, 21 Jan 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: The impact assessment of high-impact AI must cover: affected persons/groups; affected fundamental rights; content and scope of social and economic impacts; usage patterns; quantitative and qualitative metrics and methods used; measures to prevent and mitigate risks and recover losses; and, where needed, an improvement plan. The operator may conduct it itself or commission a third party; the Minister notifies other matters.
what_is_tested: Fundamental rights impact assessment content and method

framework: NCA 'Draft of AI Cybersecurity Guidelines' (AICG-1:2026), draft for public consultation (closed 5 Aug 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct a cybersecurity risk assessment that classifies AI agents' actions by potential impact, likelihood and reversibility, and apply appropriate safeguards.
what_is_tested: Cybersecurity risk of AI agent actions

framework: Singapore AI Verify Testing Framework (for traditional and generative AI; updated 2025-05-29)
requirement_paraphrase: Assess risks and risk levels per use case; continuously assess, measure and monitor outcomes and risks including after deployment; identify and document TEVV considerations (experimental design, data representativeness, construct validity).
what_is_tested: Use-case risk assessment, ongoing monitoring, TEVV documentation

framework: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard V1 (Oct 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems rated high risk must undergo conformity assessments both before and after deployment, coordinated with DoH's Data and Digital Governance Office.
what_is_tested: Conformity with ethical standards and statutory requirements

framework: ADGM Office of Data Protection - Guidance on DPR 2021 Part 4 (DPIA)
requirement_paraphrase: Controllers must regularly review that processing still matches the DPIA, and must notify the Commissioner before go-live if high risk remains after mitigation.
what_is_tested: Ongoing alignment of processing with DPIA; residual risk

framework: Dubai AI Integration Matrix Framework for Government Organizations (Dubai Digital Authority, August 2025, Version 1.0 per front matter; earlier listing date 28 Apr 2026 conflicts)
clause_or_page: Ch. 10.3 (AI Ethics Policy) and 10.2 (Initiative Approval), printed p. 87
requirement_paraphrase: States that every AI initiative under DDA must demonstrate alignment with DDA's ethical principles and undergo rigorous validation for ethical compliance across its lifecycle, and passes a standard approval workflow including technical feasibility, business case, risk evaluation and resource sign-off.
what_is_tested: Ethical compliance validation; initiative risk evaluation

framework: Information Security Regulation v2.0 (DESC)
requirement_paraphrase: Organisations carry out suitable security testing of information systems during development (control text has no modal verb).
what_is_tested: Security of information systems under development
who_tests: Dubai Government Entity (control owner); DESC sets the regulation

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
clause_or_page: Unnumbered bullet on p.22, immediately before heading s3.2.2.3 (external audit for critical decisions); layout ambiguous
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems informing significant decisions should be subject to quality checks.
what_is_tested: Quality of AI-informed significant decisions

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.4.4 (s2.4 Operational Security), printed p.14
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must secure its AI/ML systems through comprehensive testing and validation that gives assurance of their resilience against potential threats.
what_is_tested: Security and resilience of AI/ML systems against threats
who_tests: The entity in scope under s1.2: ministries and federal authorities and non-government CII entities; for emirate government entities verifiers read s1.2 differently (directly only where no emirate CIIP programme exists, or directly or through the Emirate Lead). See UAE-Federal-P3-08.

framework: UK AI Security Institute (AISI)
requirement_paraphrase: AISI states it tests leading AI systems before they are released and collaborates with AI companies, with pre-deployment access to leading models; it open-sources evaluation tools such as Inspect.
what_is_tested: Pre-release testing of frontier models

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Identify and document scientific integrity and TEVV considerations, including experimental design, data collection/selection (representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness and construct validation.
what_is_tested: Validity of test design and data

framework: US NIST AI 800-2 ipd (CAISI) Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models (Initial Public Draft, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Report qualified claims: distinguish observations, inferences, predictions and normative statements and tie claims to the evaluated benchmark and measurement conditions.
what_is_tested: Calibration of claims from test results
